r2_smallest_rectangle2 — 2D region op

• Data kinds: region → region

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "r2_smallest_rectangle2", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: smallest_rectangle2 (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

Usage

Minimum-area ORIENTED bounding rectangle as a mask (rotating calipers).

Draws, as a mask, the rotated rectangle of minimum area containing all foreground pixels of the region. It takes the convex hull of the foreground coordinates, builds a circumscribed rectangle oriented parallel to each edge of the hull, and picks the one with the smallest area (rotating calipers; uses the property that a minimum-area rectangle touches one of the hull's edges). The internal representation is the centre (cy, cx), the long side long_len, the short side short_len, and the orientation of the long side angle (radians measured in image coordinates x=col, y=row).

a stretches only the long side by a factor of 1 + 0.3*a (a=0 gives the minimum rectangle itself, a=1 a long side 1.3 times as long; the short side is unchanged). b is unused. Drawing uses the projections from the centre |pu| <= long/2 + 0.5, |pv| <= short/2 + 0.5, adding a margin of 0.5 pixel for the extent of a pixel, so the output always contains the input region.

The return value is a float64 0/1 mask of the same shape as the input; all zeros if there is no foreground. The numerical values of angle and side lengths are not returned. If there are several connected components, there is 1 rectangle for the whole. If the foreground is 1 pixel or lies on a straight line, the rectangle degenerates (point or line segment) and the drawing becomes a thin band about 1 pixel wide. If axis-parallel suffices, r2_smallest_rectangle1 is lighter. Used as preprocessing for checking the orientation of elongated parts, or for judging rectangularity by the area ratio with r2_inner_rectangle1.

Border handling: treat everything outside the image as background (0) (measured; tools/impl2/border_probe.py).
